newsitem.title: USA: Horse patrol, more agents for U.S.-Mexican border.
newsitem.headline: Horse patrol, more agents for U.S.-Mexican border.

text.p: A drive on illegal immigration across the California-Mexico border will be beefed up with 200 more agents, a horse patrol and underground sensors, the Clinton administration said on Thursday.

Doris Meissner, commissioner of the Immigration and Naturalisation Service, said the area would also get 6.5 miles (10.5 km) of new fencing, six new infrared scopes, road improvements to make the terrain more accessible to Border Patrol agents and two fixed-wing aircraft for surveillance.

Her announcement at a news conference near the border came on the second anniversary of Operation Gatekeeper, the administration's effort to keep people from illegally entering California from Mexico.

Since the operation began in October 1994, illegal traffic has been moving further east of San Diego, through rough, mountainous terrain. Earlier this year, the INS poured extra agents and equipment into that area, east of Otay Mountain. Meissner said the most recent effort would increase help for the area.

Noting that arrests of illegal immigrants in Imperial Beach to the west were drastically down because of earlier efforts, Meissner said, "We will continue to build on these accomplishments and establish control in East County."

In addition to 200 more agents from next week, Meissner said there would be a horse patrol team for the rugged back country and 264 underground sensors to detect people trying to sneak across the border.
Since the inception of Operation Gatekeeper, the number of Border Patrol agents in the county has doubled, from 980 to 1,947.

U.S. Attorney Alan Bersin also promised stepped-up prosecution of immigrant-smugglers, known as "coyotes," while Meissner said the Border Patrol would operate highway checkpoints on major roads in the area round-the-clock.

Meissner said the INS was also making efforts to warn immigrants trying to cross in East County of the dangerous terrain and extreme temperatures they were likely to encounter. She said the Mexican government had proposed doing the same.
